claims.text: Nutrition: do a careful nutritional assessment, esp if breastfeed was ⍉well established b4 hsp d/c.
claims.quote: Perform a careful nutritional assessment at this visit, particularly if breastfeeding was not well established before hospital discharge.

claims.text: Birth wt: likely ⍉regained until 7 to 14 days after birth, esp in breastfed newborns.
claims.quote: Birth weight will likely not be regained until 7 to 14 days after birth, particularly for breastfed newborns.

claims.text: Wt loss >10% of birth wt: needs further eval.
claims.quote: Weight loss of >10% of birth weight requires further evaluation.

claims.text: Jaundice: often assoc w dehydration and hypernatremia; assess overall hydration, esp in breastfed newborns.
claims.quote: Jaundice, which is often associated with dehydration and hypernatremia. Overall hydration, particularly for breastfed newborns.

claims.text: Urine output: by day 4 or 5, a newborn should pass 6 or more clear, dilute urines each day.
claims.quote: Urine may initially be dark or contain uric acid crystals, but by day 4 or 5, a newborn should pass 6 or more clear, dilute urines each day.

claims.text: Stools: initial meconium may be unrelated to feeding, but the transition to human milk stool = a key indicator of intake.
claims.quote: Initial elimination of meconium may be unrelated to feeding, but the transition to human milk stool is a key indicator of intake.

claims.text: Breastfed stools: well-nourished breastfed newborns USU pass a medium-sized yellow stool ± 3 to 4 ×/day, or as often as w every feeding.
claims.quote: Well-nourished breastfed newborns usually pass a medium-sized yellow stool at least 3 to 4 times per day, or as often as with every feeding.

claims.text: Food insecurity: screen w the validated 2-question Hunger Vital Sign tool.
claims.quote: Screen for food insecurity using the validated 2-question Hunger Vital Sign tool.

claims.text: Develop surveillance — social and language: sustains periods of wakefulness for feeding; brief eye contact w an adult when held; cries w discomfort; calms to an adult's voice.
claims.quote: Social Language and Self-help Does your child • Sustain periods of wakefulness for feeding? • Make brief eye contact with adult when held? Verbal Language (Expressive and Receptive) Does she • Cry with discomfort? • Calm to adult's voice?
claims.locator: First Week Visit (3 to 5 Days), Surveillance of Development

claims.text: Develop surveillance — motor: lifts head briefly when on stomach and turns it to the side; moves arms and legs symmetrically and reflexively when startled; keeps hands in a fist.
claims.quote: Gross Motor Does he • Lift his head briefly when on his stomach and turn it to the side? • Move his arms and legs symmetrically and reflexively when startled? Fine Motor Does she • Keep her hands in a fist?
claims.locator: First Week Visit (3 to 5 Days), Surveillance of Development

claims.text: Parent-newborn interaction — observe: do parents and newborn respond to each other (gazing, talking, smiling, holding, cuddling, comforting, showing affection); do the parents appear content and @ ease or depressed, tearful, angry, anxious, fatigued, overwhelmed; are they aware of and effective in responding to the newborn's distress; are they confident in holding, comforting, feeding and reading the newborn's cues; do both parents support each other.
claims.quote: Observation focuses on • Do the parents and newborn respond to each other (gazing, talking, smiling, holding, cuddling, comforting, showing affection)? • Do the parents appear content, happy, at ease, depressed, tearful, angry, anxious, fatigued, overwhelmed, or uncomfortable? • Are the parents aware of, responsive to, and effective in responding to the newborn's distress? • Do the parents appear confident in holding, comforting, feeding, and understanding the newborn's cues or behaviors? • What are the parents' and newborn's interactions around comforting, dressing, changing diapers, and feeding? • Are both parents present and do they support each other or show signs of disagreement?
claims.locator: First Week Visit (3 to 5 Days), Observation of Parent-Newborn Interaction
